title: G-L2 criterion A FAIL read-only RCA: 5 one-byte rgb mismatches are caused by one extra normalization in the mesh normal chain (H2, source-level); site = render_math.cu:239 + render_common.cu:200 vs upstream ray.py:727-729

attribution_correction.seg_semantics: seg = (objid, objtype); seg[1] is the MuJoCo object type, NOT the geom type
attribution_correction.wrong_reading_rejected: geom_type 5 would be CYLINDER (mat-green/ramp); dump attribution.geom_type took seg[1] and is mislabelled; rename to objtype listed for errata
attribution_correction.dump_side_note: tests/support/render_bvh/light/diag.rs segment_attribution() names seg[1] as geom_type

steps: rebuild the camera-space ray from dump direction bits + camera pose bits (offset 0)
map to geom 3 local frame with state.npz geom_xpos/geom_xmat bits (mat_t_vec order pinned as in the product)
run warp intersect_ray_tri_woop (diff_product, fma emulated exactly via float64) over the 4 mesh triangles; pick nearest t
compute depth = t * (-dir_local.z) (product write path) and compare with the dumped reference depth bits
independently cross-check the hit (face/uv/t) in float64
recompute the shading normal under both chains: upstream normalize(mat @ cross) vs product normalize(mat @ normalize(cross))

replay_validation.note: the 1-ULP offsets are replay-contraction artefacts; product-vs-reference depth is bit-identical at these pixels (dump depth.ulp = 0), which is what excludes the intersection side

root_cause.verdict_meaning: source-level structural difference (one extra normalization), not a compiler-version/libdevice difference
root_cause.primary_site: src/render/kernel/cuda/render_math.cu:239 + src/render/kernel/cuda/render_common.cu:200 (product normalizes twice) vs mujoco_warp/_src/ray.py:727-729 (upstream normalizes once)
root_cause.product_chain: mesh_query_ray: *out_normal = normalize3_mesh(min_normal); then ray_mesh_leaf: *normal = normalize3_mesh(mat_vec(mat, n_local)) => normalize(mat @ normalize(cross))
root_cause.upstream_chain: warp intersect_ray_tri_woop returns the unnormalized cross(ab, ac); ray_mesh_with_bvh then does normal = mat @ n; normal = wp.normalize(normal) => normalize(mat @ cross)
root_cause.relation: the extra normalization changes the pre-vertex-normal normal by 1 ULP; because vertex_normal() rejects 2 of 3 vertex normals on this face, the face normal dominates the interpolated shading normal, which then differs by 1 ULP
root_cause.scope: mesh-only (and hfield/SDF share the path; absent in this scene)

mechanism.consequence: two of the three interpolation weights use the face normal, so the pre-normal difference propagates into the shading normal
mechanism.byte_flip: 1-ULP normal change propagates through lighting (specular pow(ndoth, 76.8) amplifies) and flips one byte only at rgb quantization boundaries
mechanism.channel_pattern: 3 of 5 flips are in B, 2 in G; G is texture-invariant for this checker (G=0.15 in both texels), so the G flips prove the difference is in lighting (normal), not in texture sampling
mechanism.camera_pattern: cam0 shows no mismatch because the mesh is not visible there (only floor + background)
mechanism.legacy_pattern: legacy/ v2.2 rgb tolerance is <= 1 LSB, so a one-byte difference was tolerated there; spec v3 criterion A requires 0 bytes (section 13 risk 10 pre-declared this exact risk)
mechanism.expected_count_check: face-2 pixels per world = 16,515 with ~1 ULP final-normal difference; boundary probability x specular amplification predicts ~1-4 flips per world; observed 2 / 3 / 0

h1_refutation: the difference is a concrete source-structure difference (one extra normalize), not the same expression compiled differently

product dot/mat/normalize helper orders (dot3_ba, mat_vec, mat_t_vec, normalize3_rays) are pinned from prior empirical RCa and reproduce the reference depth to <= 1 ULP in this replay, so they are not the site
a pure compiler-version difference cannot explain why the normal bits differ at exactly the mesh-only chain and at 5/5 mismatched pixels

fix_direction.minimal: make the mesh normal chain match upstream: return the unnormalized triangle cross from the mesh query (render_math.cu:239) and keep the single normalize after the geom transform (render_common.cu:200)
fix_direction.culling_note: culling uses the dot sign only; normalization does not change the sign
fix_direction.shadow_note: shadow origin = hit + normal*1e-4 becomes upstream-identical as a side effect

impact.refreeze: required (12 frozen exes + new PTX baseline)
impact.window: one full G-L2 window re-run (1 slice + 1 window)
impact.signature: none: criteria / reference / spec / signed material unchanged; no user signature required

fix_direction.suggested_order: diagnostic round with the patched entity exe (not G-L2 evidence, no refreeze) to confirm the 5 pixels go to zero, then the formal refreeze + attempt3

risks: product woop intersection does not implement upstream's double-precision recompute of U/V/W when any of them is exactly zero (render_math.cu:100-108 comment); excluded this time because product-vs-reference depth bits are identical at all 5 pixels (that branch would change t), but it stays a latent alignment gap
criterion B, two-run sha and world isolation were not evaluated in this run (the assertion aborted earlier); this card makes no statement about them
if the fix still leaves a few one-byte differences, the same method (depth-bit validation + normal bit diff) should be repeated for the remaining normalization/contraction sites
non_claim: does not claim G-L2 pass, criterion A/B/C satisfaction, upstream equivalence, or any render numeric conclusion
does not change any criterion, threshold, reference, spec, frozen artefact or window state
the fix direction is registered only; this card does not implement it
